name: Question 8
problem: A tutoring center currently has $10$ enrolled students. The number of students in the center $T(t)$ increases at a rate that obeys an inhibited growth model, where $t\ge 0$ is the time in months. If the maximum capacity of the tutoring center is $95$ students, which differential equation could be used to model the student population of the center? Assume that $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality.

html:
Question 8
?

A tutoring center currently has 10 enrolled students. The number of students in the center T(t) increases at a rate that obeys an inhibited growth model, where t≥0 is the time in months. If the maximum capacity of the tutoring center is 95 students, which differential equation could be used to model the student population of the center? Assume that k>0 is a constant of proportionality.

a
dTdt=k(30−T)
b
dTdt=k(60−T)
c
dTdt=k(95−T)
d
dTdt=k(950−T)
e
dTdt=k(100−T)
Submit
